- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.5) and forecast is rising, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% to avoid overcorrection.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+2.0% from prior day), cap forecast increase to avoid overshoot; allow 1–2 days of lagged mean reversion.  
- If sentiment turns positive (e.g., >0.1) and forecast is flat or falling, increase forecast by 0.5–1.0% to capture momentum.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome exceeds forecast by >1.5% for 3+ consecutive days, adjust next forecast downward by 0.5–1.0% to avoid overestimating continuation.  
- If sentiment is consistently negative and price is trending upward, treat as “mean reversion bias” — reduce forecast by 0.3–0.7% per day until sentiment reverses.
